why: `src/` with an `__init__.py` is a package, imported from the repository root as `from src.services.x import …`. The src-layout rule used to strip `src.` from every module id regardless, so the ids and the imports named the same modules differently and nothing joined: a field report (3.42.0) had 33 of 34 modules imported by nothing and `src/__init__.py` named `py:<root>`. The ids here keep `src.`, because that is the name Python resolves.
excluded: The package `__init__` modules import nothing, so they carry no IMPORTS edges; they are labelled only as Module nodes.
